summary: Iteration 17 — Partner Payment Gateway (MidGate as PG for first-party 'midnight' app). Backend: 19/19 pytest passing covering admin partner CRUD, list/detail with stats+charges+deliveries, PATCH webhook_url, rotate-key, rotate-secret, deactivate/reactivate, Bearer auth on /api/pay/* (missing/bad/inactive → 401), RBAC (teammate 403 on /api/admin/partners), charge create returns real Mayar checkout link (myr.id), idempotency on same reference_id, amount min/max (400) and blank/missing reference_id (422), spoofed public Mayar webhook does NOT flip pending→paid (server re-verifies with Mayar), and DELETE partner cascades. Frontend: admin console → /admin/partners → New partner dialog → credentials-once view (mgpay_live_/mgwhsec_ visible) → row appears → Manage dialog (Configuration+Save, Rotate API key reveals new key, Deactivate/Activate toggle, stats + Charges + Webhook deliveries sections) → Delete removes row. No console page errors. All QA-created partners cleaned up (list empty).

minor.issue: Partner-supplied customer.name (min 3 chars) and customer.mobile (min 10 chars) are forwarded to Mayar unmodified. Reasonable-looking-but-short inputs (e.g. name='A', mobile='0812' from the review spec) trigger a Mayar 400 which we surface as a 502 to the partner. Recommend either (a) padding/defaulting when the field is too short (like email fallback already does) or (b) validating in the Pydantic ChargeCreate model so partners get a clear 422 instead of a 502.

action_items: Pad or validate short customer.name/mobile in /api/pay/charges so partners never see a 502 from Mayar's min-length validation.
critical_code_review_comments: partner_pay._settle uses find_one_and_update with a status filter to atomically claim the paid transition — good; prevents double-delivery.

webhook_secret is stored in plaintext in the partners collection (not hashed). Rotate flow works but if the DB is dumped, secrets leak. Consider hashing (bcrypt/scrypt) and verifying via HMAC helper that fetches at delivery time — acceptable for first-party only but worth noting.
Public /api/wallet/mayar/webhook handler forwards unmatched events to partner_pay.handle_mayar_event which re-verifies with Mayar before flipping paid — verified safe against spoofed events.

Idempotency is enforced by unique (partner_id, reference_id) index + application-level early return; a burst of duplicate POSTs will race on Mayar invoice creation before the unique index catches — consider guarding with an insert-first pattern to avoid orphaned Mayar invoices on rapid duplicates.
get_partner accepts key via Authorization: Bearer OR X-Partner-Key header — documented behavior, fine.
resend endpoint correctly gates on status=='paid' to prevent leaking unpaid webhooks.
seed_data_creation: None persistent — all QA partners created during tests were deleted (verified list empty after run). Operator can safely create the real 'midnight' partner.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter 17 covers partner payment gateway only. Wallet/top-up (iter 16) not retested. Paid→signed-webhook→delivery-log path was pre-verified manually by main agent (charge flipped in DB, resend to httpbin returned 200 and logged). test_iteration_17_partners.py is now a stable regression suite — runs in ~15s and uses real Mayar production invoice creation (harmless unpaid invoices). If Mayar throttles or is unreachable, the create/idempotent/webhook-safety tests will fail with 502; the rest are independent.
rca of the issue: Minor 502 on short customer fields: mayar.create_invoice returns 400 Validation Error for name<3 chars / mobile<10 chars. partner_pay.create_charge catches MayarError and returns HTTPException(502, 'Could not create payment'). Fix: add min_length constraints on Customer.name/mobile in ChargeCreate or pad values before calling mayar (mirrors existing email fallback).
